items.body:
> **Anchors in this issue are cited against `da4e444`.** Main is now `6e75c6d`; #240, #246, #247, #252 and #253 merged since. Resolve line numbers against `da4e444`, not against main — the rebase note in the comments says what moved.

*Evidence verified against `main` @ `da4e444` (PR #239, merged 2026-09-02, moved lines in `backend/app/models/schema.py`, `backend/app/catalog/service.py` and `docs/posture-snapshot.md`; the citations into those files are post-#239, every other cited file is unchanged since `82aed70`). Split from #81 (v0 blocker 1), which stays the contract record. This session runs first; #242 runs second and reads the payload this issue defines. #243 is independent of both; `key_bundle` is v1 (#245).*

## Why now

Every ruling the snapshot needed is now on the record, and the thing itself is not built. #81 ruling 1 — one event per installed app, Jamf's object untouched — has stood since 2026-08-24. The vocabulary it travels under was frozen on 2026-09-01 (#188, PR #228, `docs/splunk-wire-vocabulary.md`); the meta block and the envelope it rides shipped in PR #191 (`_device_meta`, `backend/app/mdm/service.py:812-870`; `backend/app/core/wire.py`) and reached every family in PR #204. Kyle answered the two questions that gated the build on 2026-09-02 — Jamf's v4 names verbatim, and fatten at enqueue — and both are recorded on #81's ruling comment (the 2026-09-02 rulings).

What is missing is the event the fan-out expands. `_build_body` cannot expand what it does not receive — it sees the destination and the stored payload and nothing else (`backend/app/core/outbox.py:109-143`) — and today the payload is a delta that exists only when an app moved. So #242 is blocked on this, #222 is blocked on the fan-out, and #81 carries `v0-blocker` until both merge. The flip is ~2026-09-17.

## What ships today

`process_sync` (`backend/app/mdm/service.py:873`) emits one event, `device.inventory.changed`, and only when the app list moved:

```python
    if not added and not removed_rows:
        await db.commit()
        return None
```
`backend/app/mdm/service.py:992-994`

A device whose apps did not change produces nothing. `test_a_sync_enqueues_one_event_per_changed_device_and_nothing_for_the_rest` (`backend/tests/test_outbox_passes_db.py:545-575`) pins the second sweep of an unchanged fleet at zero device events, and its docstring calls that "the number #81 rewrites"; `test_wire_casing.py:161-175` has to move an app on purpose just to get an inventory event to judge. The one event that does exist carries `addedApps`/`removedApps` as `NormalizedApp` lists — `name`, `bundleId`, `version`, `shortVersion` (always null from the Jamf normalizer, `backend/app/mdm/jamf/client.py:737-741`) plus the four minted identity fields (`backend/app/schemas/payload.py:31-53`) — and `deviceMeta` (`payload.py:133`). `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` has four members (`outbox.py:21`); a type not in it can be neither produced nor subscribed to (`outbox.py:23`, `backend/app/schemas/destinations.py:55-61`).

No *state* event on the wire today carries `path`, `cfBundleShortVersionString`, `cfBundleVersion` or `macAppStore`, and none carries any section other than applications. (`device.change` does carry them — the canonical entry body as `old`/`new` on an application change, and per-field values for the scalar sections: `backend/app/changes/derive.py:148-158`, `:192-204`, `:311-318` — but that family says what happened, not what is, #81 ruling 6, and it is not the family this issue adds to.)

## What is ruled, and where — not re-litigated here

| Ruling | Record |
| --- | --- |
| One snapshot stream, per app; Jamf's object untouched | #81 ruling 1 |
| Jamf's v4 names, verbatim. Kyle, 2026-09-02: "Use Jamf's v4 Names Verbatim in the sections I am copying them." Kyle, 2026-09-01: "I leave the jamf data as is when copying it over to the record under the `apps` key so leave as is. I don't want to change that or take on that ETL work." He ruled the *names*; the field set is the next row | #81 ruling comment, 2026-09-02 |
| Fatten at enqueue; no delivery-time join. Kyle, 2026-09-02: "flatten at enqueue" — read as *fatten*, the option he confirmed on 2026-09-01 with "both answers aren't great, but I think that is the better one." | #81 ruling comment, 2026-09-02; #81 spike comment Q2 |
| Field set on the app object = the ledger's allowlist: `name`, `path`, `version`, `cfBundleShortVersionString`, `cfBundleVersion`, `bundleId`, `macAppStore`. `sizeMegabytes`, `updateAvailable`, `externalVersionId` stay off. A **labelled assumption**, not his words — the spike's sub-decision A (telemetry rides) was not separately accepted | `backend/app/mdm/jamf/contract.py:322-336`; #81 ruling comment (recorded there as an assumption) |
| Wrapper keys and sourcetypes: the frozen registry, generated from `SECTIONS` | `docs/splunk-wire-vocabulary.md` §2; `backend/app/core/wire_vocabulary.py:46-63` |
| `patch` and `vuln` are inline enrichments on the app sub-event | `wire_vocabulary.py:65-75` |
| `patch.supported`: a bool, always present, `false` when no Jamf Patch title matches. Kyle, 2026-09-01: "we need a default for the patching... Probably a boolean that says `patchingSupport` and set that equal to false. That way you can always search for it or not it easy." | #81 ruling comment, 2026-09-02 |
| `vuln.assessment` ∈ `covered` \| `unknown_app` \| `off`, always present; ships `off` until #113's work lands | #113, ruled 2026-09-01; #81 ruling comment |
| The minted identity fields (`appHash`, `versionHash`, `keyTitle`, `keyFull`) do not ride the sub-events in v0. Kyle, 2026-09-02: "leave them out for now we can add them in the future. We can add keys later but we can't take them away." | #81 ruling comment, 2026-09-02 |
| Aperture: `apps is None` = outside the read, touch nothing; `[]` = read and genuinely empty; read per section on the snapshot | `service.py:881-888`; `payload.py:76-79`; Kyle, 2026-08-29; #81 ruling comment |
| `deviceMeta`: the block as built, nulls dropped, `eventID = uuid5(jobID, jamfProID)` | `service.py:812-870`; `docs/runs.md:107-130`. #189 owns the block, including any drift between its 2026-08-31 table and what is built; nothing here adds or moves a key |
| Envelope: `time` from the event's own timestamp, `host` in both places on purpose, `source` = the instance | `wire.py:68-91`; `outbox.py:121-130` |
| Casing: camelCase, the token `ID` uppercase, a vendor's key keeps the vendor's spelling | `docs/splunk-wire-vocabulary.md` §4 |
| Additive-only clauses 1–6 | `wire_vocabulary.py:118-133` |

## The design

### One event, `device.inventory`

One `device.inventory` per device per ingest that passes the ledger's monotonic guard, whether or not anything changed. It fires from `process_sync`, in the same transaction as the ledger write and the row updates — `ingest_computer` promises exactly that (`service.py:644-645`), and so does `enqueue_event` (`outbox.py:75-77`). It does **not** fire on the stale path (`service.py:657-672` returns before `process_sync` is reached), and not for a device whose ingest raised and was rolled back (`service.py:527-533`).

The name is a recommendation, not a ruling. `device.inventory` is the state; `device.inventory.changed` is what happened to it — #81 ruling 6's IS/HAPPENED test applied to the discriminator — so the delta keeps its name and keeps shipping unchanged, which is what generic webhooks and change derivation were promised in #81's body. `event` stays the one discriminator on every family (`docs/runs.md:142-148`); `event=device.inventory*` then collects the state and its deltas together and `event=device.inventory.changed` is untouched. Alternatives the session may prefer, named so they are rejected rather than missed: `device.inventory.snapshot` (says what it is, but pairs oddly with `.changed` as a sibling suffix on the same noun) and `device.snapshot` (drops the noun the delta family already uses).

### The payload — proposed shape; the session finalises it inside the rulings

```json
{
  "event": "device.inventory",
  "occurredAt": "2026-09-02T02:00:00+00:00",
  "deviceMeta": { "jobID": "…", "trigger": "sweep", "eventID": "…", "…": "the built #189 block, unchanged" },

  "general":         { "…": "Jamf's object, Jamf's keys, the contract's allowlist" },
  "hardware":        { "…": "…" },
  "operatingSystem": { "…": "…" },
  "userAndLocation": { "…": "…" },
  "purchasing":      { "…": "…" },
  "security":        { "…": "…" },
  "diskEncryption":  { "…": "…" },

  "app": [
    { "app":   { "name": "Maps.app", "path": "/System/Applications/Maps.app", "version": "3.0",
                 "cfBundleShortVersionString": "3.0", "cfBundleVersion": "2972.20.6.12.13",
                 "bundleId": "com.apple.Maps", "macAppStore": false },
      "patch": { "supported": false },
```

1. **The wrapper keys are the registry's and nothing else.** Fourteen possible section keys, exactly `SECTION_WRAPPERS.values()` (`wire_vocabulary.py:46-63`): the seven scalar sections are objects, the seven list sections are lists. The registry's own comment groups `localUserAccount` under "one per device — long" (`wire_vocabulary.py:47-55`); that is the naming rule, and the contract's `entry_kind` makes it a list (`contract.py:425-428`) — the list wins. The scalar ones are what #81 called the "device anchor" — under the frozen registry the anchor is not one sub-event but one per scalar section (`loon:jamf:mac:general`, `…:hardware`, and so on), which is why all seven ride here.
2. **A list item is the sub-event body, minus `deviceMeta`.** `{"app": {…Jamf…}, "patch": {…}, "vuln": {…}}` is, byte for byte, what #242 emits under `loon:jamf:mac:app` once it adds the block, the envelope and (its decision D1) the `event` key — so the fan-out is iteration, not reshaping, and every shape decision lives on this side of the outbox, where the data is. It also keeps LoonInspect's enrichment keys *beside* Jamf's object rather than inside it: the standing "namespaced, not flattened" answer (`docs/splunk-wire-vocabulary.md:44-47`), and the guarantee that Jamf can never add a field that collides with `patch`. The price is `app[].app.bundleId` on a generic-webhook or Elastic document. The alternative — bare Jamf objects in the list, with the fan-out hoisting enrichment keys back out of them — puts the same decision in two places. Session's call; written down so it is a decision.
3. **Jamf's names; the allowlist's fields.** Every section object is Jamf's v4 object under Jamf's keys, restricted to the contract's allowlist for that section (`contract.py:199-397`). For the app object this is the reading #81's comment records, labelled as an assumption: Kyle ruled the *names*; the field set is the reading of "leave the jamf data as is", and the one point he may want to overrule. For the other thirteen sections it is a second labelled **assumption**: "in the sections I am copying them" read as the same rule everywhere — Jamf's names, not Jamf's every field. Consequence worth saying out loud: the telemetry the allowlist excludes (`lastContactTime`, `lastIpAddress`, `reportDate`, battery — `contract.py:222-225`, `:253-254`; disk free is a section v0 never reads, `contract.py:26-28`) is off the wire in v0. 4. **Labelled entries carry their label under Jamf's key.** The contract keeps names out of the *hash* — "names of Jamf objects are labels, not content" (`contract.py:29-34`) — and carries them beside the body as `Entry.label` (`contract.py:527-531`). The wire wants the name: `ea.name`, `group.groupName`, `profile.displayName` are what an analyst types. So the item is the entry body plus the label under the key Jamf spells it with (`entry_label`, `contract.py:415-423`). This is what #197 asks of the EA object — keyed on `definitionId`, with `name` carried as the label (#197: "the contract keys on `definitionId`", and name "is the label").

A section wrapper absent: the section was outside this read's aperture — a second meaning for a missing key beside clause 4's single one, "Absence of a key means the event predates it, never that its value is 'none'" (`wire_vocabulary.py:125-127`; `docs/splunk-wire-vocabulary.md:142-144`). ### The four fields the installed-apps table does not hold — the decision, with a recommendation and the trade

`installed_apps` holds `name`, `bundle_id`, `version`, `short_version`, the hashes and the patch columns (`schema.py:187-226`) — no `path`, `cfBundleShortVersionString`, `cfBundleVersion`, `macAppStore`. Two sources were on the table:

**(a) Read the canonical observation.** The entry bodies at `observation.sections["applications"].entries[*].body` hold at most the seven allowlisted fields, each absent where Jamf sent null or omitted it. Free: no schema change, no second write path, the object already in hand, and a payload that is self-contained — it never couples the wire to ledger retention (`docs/jamf-observations.md:309` reserves the right to compact). Trade: the values are the ledger's canonical form, not Jamf's raw bytes — NFC-normalised and stripped strings (`contract.py:75-76`), every spelling of absence dropped (`:114-140`; one app in the real fixture, `BambuStudio.app`, reports `"cfBundleVersion": null`, which becomes an absent key), byte-identical entries collapsed (`:525-526`), digest order rather than Jamf's order (`:532`). Against the 83 apps of `computer_inventory_detail_real.json` none of that changes a single string value; it can, in principle. The reading of "as is" this rests on is *names and field set*, which is the reading #81's ruling comment records.

**(b) Four new columns** on `installed_apps`, written at `service.py:968-981`. Trade: a migration, ~100 rows × four columns per device for data nothing but the wire reads, and a third copy of bytes `observation_entries` already stores once per tenant (`schema.py:957-972`). Decisive against it: columns solve the app section only. The other thirteen wrappers have no rows to read — `Device` holds a dozen scalars (`schema.py:128-153`) and there is no certificates or profiles table — so (b) needs (a) for everything else anyway.

**Recommend (a).** The snapshot is one object, read from one place, and it agrees with the ledger byte for byte — which is what makes a `device.inventory` sub-event and a `device.change` derived from the same span (#223) join on equal strings. If the session judges "as is" to mean Jamf's bytes, the variant is (a′): apply the same allowlist to `raw` with the contract's own selector (`_select`, `contract.py:153-174`) and skip `_prune`; same field set, raw values, empty strings kept — at the cost of re-implementing the EA merge and quarantine (`:543-563`) for the wire, which is the two-copies failure #197 exists to end.

## Storage, retention and the worker — the consequences, measured where I could

**Size.** Built from `computer_inventory_detail_real.json` through the contract's own canonicalizer (`canonicalize_computer`, imported directly), under the full aperture, in the shape above, as compact JSON: **28,234 bytes** for one device with a synthetic thirteen-key `deviceMeta`. The fixture-derived halves are exact — 22,324 bytes of `app` list (83 items at ~269 bytes each, ~204 for Jamf's seven fields and ~65 for the two enrichment blocks) and 5,304 bytes for the other thirteen sections together; the ~430-byte head (`event`, `occurredAt`, `deviceMeta`) varies with the meta values. The same device's delta event on a baseline sweep is ~26.3 KB by the README's own arithmetic (509 + 311 × 83 = 26,322, `README.md:13`). So a snapshot costs roughly what a baseline costs today — **every sweep, not once**. It is the spike's 25–35 KB estimate, now measured on one real record.

**Outbox.** At the codebase's own design target of 40,000 devices (`outbox.py:30-31`, `:44-46`): ~1.1 GB of JSONB per sweep; a nightly sweep under the default `event_outbox_retention_days = 7` (`backend/app/core/config.py:45`, purged from `backend/app/main.py:215`) steady-states around 8 GB of rows in `event_outbox` before TOAST compression, which I did not measure. At 5,000 devices: ~140 MB a sweep, ~1 GB resident. `README.md:13` — "a quiet day afterwards is roughly 4 MB" — stops being true for any destination that receives the snapshot.

**What #213 already bounded** (merged as `7bd4d30`): both worker ticks take at most 1,000 rows, oldest first (`outbox.py:58`, `:283-286`, `:345-350`). What #213 deliberately left for "#81's work": `fan_out_pending` still selects every column, payload included, to flip a boolean (`:283-286`; pinned at `test_outbox_passes_db.py:402-430`, the `"event_outbox.payload" in selects[0]` assertion at `:427`) — at 28 KB a row, ~28 MB through the worker every thirty seconds for the twenty minutes a 40k backlog takes to fan out. **Narrowing that select is not this session's.** It has its own seam, its own pinned test and its own prior deferral — `id` and `event_type` in, `fanned_out` flipped by id, `:402-430` rewritten to pin the narrow shape — so it is split out as #244 rather than ridden here as a checklist item, landing before or with #242, where a 40k backlog's width is paid. Delivery throughput — 1,000 sequential POSTs a tick, 10 s timeout each (`:312-317`) — is #242's problem, with HEC batching explicitly not v0 per #81.

**What #154/#156 pinned** (`backend/tests/test_outbox_passes_db.py`, header docstring): who gets a delivery row, the passes' SQL shape, producer volume, delivery bookkeeping, retention. The producer-volume test is the one this session rewrites on purpose; the rest should pass untouched.

**The disabled-destination edge, from the spike.** `deliver_pending` leaves a disabled destination's deliveries `pending` so re-enabling resumes them (`outbox.py:386-390`); `purge_delivered_events` never deletes an event that holds a pending delivery, "however old it is" (`:479-490`). Composed — `test_a_disabled_destination_makes_its_events_immortal` (`:834-859`) — switching a destination off freezes every event fanned out to it, at any age, past any retention setting. Today that is one row per changed device; after this issue it is 28 KB per device per sweep, ~1.1 GB a night at 40k. The growth is at least visible on the posture tape — `outbox.pending` counts rows holding a pending delivery and `outbox.oldest_pending_age_s` climbs (`docs/posture-snapshot.md:146-148`) — but nothing bounds it. **Recommend: not this session.** It is a retention design question (disable-with-drain, a pending-age ceiling, or "disabled means abandon"), it belongs with the outbox remedies already listed on #91, and it should be filed against #91 rather than solved in the same PR that changes the volume. Kyle can pull it forward.

- Bounding the disabled-destination growth — filed against #91, per above.
- Mobile devices. v0 reads computers only (Kyle, R1, 2026-09-01, recorded on #232); the platform segment is `mac` throughout and rides the sourcetype, never the payload.

## Ordering

This session first. #242 second — it reads this payload and cannot start before the shape is on `main`. Between the two PRs a `splunk_hec` destination receives the whole snapshot as one nested HEC event under the operator's input sourcetype (`docs/splunk-setup.md:159-170`), past the `TRUNCATE` default the setup doc already warns about (`:184-189`) — days long and pre-flip, which is why the two sessions run back to back and why `v0-blocker` stays on #81 until the fan-out PR merges. The select narrowing (#244) lands before or with the fan-out. #243 is independent of both. `key_bundle` is v1 (#245). `KP Input required` comes off #81 with its ruling comment.

## Done when

- [ ] Every ingest that passes the stale guard enqueues exactly one `device.inventory` per device, in the same transaction as the ledger write and the row updates; the stale path enqueues none. Asserted in `test_jamf_sync_e2e.py`.
- [ ] The second sweep of an unchanged fleet enqueues one snapshot per device and zero `device.inventory.changed`; the first enqueues both. Asserted in `test_outbox_passes_db.py` §3.
- [ ] Under the full aperture the snapshot's section keys equal `SECTION_WRAPPERS.values()`; under a narrowed aperture only the read sections appear; a read-and-empty list is `[]`. Asserted.
- [ ] Every `app` item is `{"app": <at most the seven allowlisted Jamf keys, absent where Jamf sent nothing>, "patch": {"supported": bool}, "vuln": {"assessment": "off"}}`; no minted identity field and no telemetry field appears; a removed app does not appear; `patch.supported` is `true` for a title-matched build whose name canonicalises differently from its raw string. Asserted against the real fixture plus that one case.
- [ ] `deviceMeta`, `occurredAt` and the `_envelope` hints on the snapshot equal the delta's for the same pull, `eventID` included. Asserted.
- [ ] `device.inventory` is in `KNOWN_EVENT_TYPES` and subscribable; the subscription default is the one decided above and `docs/splunk-setup.md` states what each destination type receives; no migration if explicit lists are left alone.
- [ ] `test_wire_casing.py` judges the fifth family and passes.
- [ ] `docs/splunk-event-shaping.md`, `docs/runs.md`, `docs/splunk-setup.md`, `README.md` and `docs/posture-snapshot.md` say what ships, at the lines above; the v4 pin and the three meanings of absence are written down, and the clause 4 decision is stated in the PR.
- [ ] `device.inventory.changed` is byte-for-byte unchanged: the e2e assertions on `addedApps`/`removedApps` (`test_jamf_sync_e2e.py:235-237`) pass untouched.

One session, `backend/` and `docs/` only.

## Where this issue is weak

- **One fixture is not a fleet.** 28 KB is one Mac mini with 83 apps, measured as compact JSON in Python, not as Postgres on-disk bytes. TOAST compression is real and unmeasured, and no Splunk licence-volume number exists yet — that number is #242's to produce with the e2e path. #220 asked for the same measurement and did not get it either.
- **The field set is an assumption twice over.** Kyle ruled the *names* for the app object; the field set — the allowlist, telemetry off — is the labelled assumption on #81's comment, against the spike's sub-decision A. "In the sections I am copying them" is then read as the same rule for the other thirteen sections, and the consequence — contact-time and IP telemetry off the wire in v0 — has not been put to him in those words. Both are additive to fix, which is why the issue proceeds rather than waits.
- **Three sections carry one field beyond the allowlist** — the entry label (`ea.name`, `group.groupName`, `profile.displayName`; `entry_label`, `contract.py:415-423`), which the three allowlists exclude by design (`contract.py:338-358`). Jamf's field under Jamf's name, so inside "names verbatim" — but outside the allowlist #81's ruling comment records as the field set. If the allowlist is the ruling, drop it and the wire ships ids without names.
- **Canonical values over raw bytes** — (a) over (a′) — is my recommendation, not a ruling. On the real fixture the two are identical; on a fleet with un-normalised app names they differ, and the hash join must be built to survive that either way. If "as is" means bytes, the session takes (a′) and pays for the duplicated EA merge.
- **The item shape** — a list of sub-event bodies, with `app[].app.*` on non-Splunk documents — is proposed here and ruled nowhere. It is the cheapest shape for the fan-out and the least pretty for a generic-webhook reader; a reviewer who weights that reader higher will prefer the other one.
- **The subscription recommendation cuts against the most recent precedent.** `run.failed` appended itself to explicit lists; this issue argues the snapshot should not. That is a judgement about what a curated list meant when it was written, and Kyle may see it the other way.
- **Session size.** Fourteen sections, the seam change, seven test files and five docs is a full session; nothing else rides in it. The select narrowing is #244; #213 already deferred it once.
- **I did not run the suite.** Every line number was read at `da4e444` — the three files PR #239 touched at that commit, the rest unchanged since `82aed70`; nothing was executed against Postgres (the DB tests need the compose network). The size figure came from a throwaway script over `canonicalize_computer`, not from the suite. The SQLAlchemy collection-after-delete hazard is stated from the library's semantics, not reproduced here.

# KF-RD-GENAI-STACK-2026-001

## Purpose
Durable research ledger for the methodical dissection of the 2026 GenAI stack and adjacent systems, followed by scientific/work-domain parallelisation and whole-system convergence into KEYFLOWOS / KEY.

This is **research and architectural memory**, not implementation authority. Production code remains untouched until findings are converged, dependency-ordered, and separately authorized for implementation.

## Required method for every subject
1. Technical dissection: architecture, primitives, algorithms, APIs, state, persistence, execution lifecycle, concurrency, failure/retry/cancellation, security, tenancy, observability, evaluation, scaling, latency, cost, DX, extensibility, licensing, known failure modes.
2. Source inspection where code is open.
3. Microscopic comparison against live KEYFLOWOS.
4. Scientific parallelisation: neuroscience, physiology, cybernetics/control theory, information theory, graph theory, distributed systems, statistics, OR, ecology/evolution, safety engineering, etc., but only where the mechanism is structurally transferable.
5. Work/operational parallelisation: medicine, aviation, finance/accounting, logistics, industrial safety, incident response, organizations, command-and-control, etc.
6. Mechanism extraction.
7. KEY/KEYFLOWOS hypothesis.
8. Experiment + measurable proof obligation.
9. Disposition: ADOPT / ADAPT / ABSORB / MERGE / REPLACE / REMOVE / BENCHMARK / WATCH / REJECT.
10. Hold findings for convergence; do not cargo-cult dependencies.

## Dual targets
Every useful finding is assessed for:
- KEY / KEYFLOWOS runtime.
- The autonomous development machinery building KEYFLOWOS (Claude Code / control plane / repo intelligence / review loops).

## Completion standard
The programme is not complete until individual subjects are researched, cross-domain mechanisms extracted, contradictions/duplicates identified, uncertain claims experimentally resolved, and the results converged into a small set of canonical architectural primitives with explicit invariants and proof obligations.

## Inventory
Layer 1: OpenAI/GPT; Anthropic/Claude; Gemini; Llama; DeepSeek; Qwen.
Layer 2: vLLM; Ollama; llama.cpp; Groq; Bedrock; Vertex AI.
Layer 3: LangChain; LangGraph; LlamaIndex; CrewAI; AutoGen; Pydantic AI.
Layer 4: OpenAI embeddings; Cohere; Voyage; Jina; BGE; Nomic.
Layer 5: Pinecone; Qdrant; Weaviate; Milvus; Chroma; pgvector.
Layer 6: Hugging Face; PEFT/LoRA; Unsloth; Axolotl; TRL; LLaMA-Factory.
Layer 7: DSPy; Instructor; Outlines; Guidance; BAML; provider structured outputs.
Layer 8: MCP; native function calling; A2A; computer/browser use; Composio; Arcade.
Layer 9: LangSmith; Langfuse; Ragas; DeepEval; Phoenix; W&B Weave.
Layer 10: NeMo Guardrails; Guardrails AI; Llama Guard; Lakera; Presidio; Rebuff.

The inventory expands when adjacent/superior systems are discovered.

## Progress
- R&D-01A OpenAI/GPT: first-pass technical dissection completed; findings held for Layer-1 convergence.
- R&D-01B Anthropic/Claude: active.

## R&D-01A — OpenAI/GPT holding findings
- Capability-based cognitive scheduling instead of model-name routing.
- Responses-style typed cognitive event streams should map underneath KEY's own lifecycle, not replace Cortex.
- Model tool selection is evidence/intent, never business-action authority.
- Machine-facing outputs should be schema-first; human presentation should not be reparsed into state.
- Hierarchical/deferred capability discovery ("capability paging") is high-value for KEY's large tool/connector surface.
- Prompt/context layout should be designed for cache locality: stable constitution -> stable business context -> semi-stable genome/session -> dynamic turn.
- Provider conversation state is ephemeral execution state, never canonical KEY memory.
- Classify AI work as realtime / interactive / background / batch / scheduled / event-triggered.
- Create a capability/lifecycle-aware model catalog.
- Current live repo gap: OpenAI path still uses Chat Completions and direct OpenAI calls exist outside the model gateway (embeddings/vision/voice/document paths); provider boundary is not yet fully converged.

## Continuity rule
Each completed subject should add a durable comment here containing:
- source-backed findings,
- current KEYFLOWOS comparison,
- science/work parallels,
- extracted mechanisms,
- candidate experiments,
- disposition,
- interactions/contradictions with earlier findings,
- implementation implications held for convergence.

At each layer boundary, publish a layer-convergence comment before proceeding to the next layer.
